narrative.title: Shipment Manifest Reconciliation
narrative.scenario: Two depots transmit their part-code lists at the end of a shift, and the receiving hub must confirm the second manifest is a rearrangement of the first — identical part codes with identical multiplicities, merely shuffled. Any mismatched count, even by a single unit, flags the shipment for manual audit. Lengths that disagree make the check fail instantly.
narrative.outputFormat: true when t is an anagram of s (same letters with the same frequencies), false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: Both manifests use each letter exactly as often as the other — a perfect rearrangement.
Same length, but the letter inventories differ: an r appears where a c should be.

hintLevels: Level 1: An anagram check is an inventory check — count every letter once and the two tallies must match exactly.
Level 2: Build one frequency map from s, then consume it while walking t: any missing letter, or a letter whose balance would go negative, fails on the spot.
Level 3: Equal lengths are necessary but nowhere near sufficient — 'aacc' and 'ccac' share a length and a letter set yet differ in counts, so only the full tally comparison settles it.
